name: Ilkal Saree Weaving Tradition (GI Tagged)
description: The distinctive handloom saree originating from Ilkal town in Bagalkote district, recognized with a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Known for its signature 'Tope Teni' technique where the red art silk/pure silk seragu (pallu) is joined with the cotton warp body using loop-jointing (Kondi technique). The saree features traditional border motifs such as Chikki Paras (dots), Gomi (chevron), and Gayatri.
cultural_origin: 8th Century CE Chalukyan patronage; sustained by Devanga and Nekara communities
technique: Pit Loom with three-shuttle weaving and Kondi pallu loop jointing
inclusive_growth_impact: Supports over 10,000 weaver families and associated allied workers (dyeing, warping, winding, Kasuti embroiderers)
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal (Handloom Tourism) & Intellectual Property India

name: Guledgudd Khana Fabric (GI Tagged)
description: India's only handwoven blouse fabric to receive a Geographical Indication tag, produced exclusively in the hill town of Guledagudda in Bagalkote district. The fabric features tightly woven cotton warp with silk/rayon extra-warp patterns forming raised geometric and auspicious motifs like Choukadi (checkered), Tulasi Katti (basil altar), Siddeshwara Pheta (turban), and Anne Kalu (elephant feet).
cultural_origin: 16th Century CE Vijayanagara & Adil Shahi eras; crafted specifically to pair with Ilkal sarees
technique: Handloom weaving on Pit and Frame Looms equipped with Dobby mechanisms for geometric patterning
inclusive_growth_impact: Vital livelihood for traditional Nekara households in Guledagudda valley; directly promoted by District Handloom Tourism Committee
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal (Handloom Tourism) & Intellectual Property India

name: Kasuti Embroidery of North Karnataka
description: A traditional, intricate hand embroidery style indigenous to North Karnataka (Bagalkote, Dharwad, and Belagavi districts). Practiced since the Chalukya period, it uses four geometric counting stitches (Gavanti, Murgi, Negi, and Menthi) without drawing patterns beforehand or making any knots, ensuring the front and back of the fabric appear identical.
cultural_origin: Patronized by Chalukya queens; traditionally embroidered on Ilkal sarees and Khana blouse fabrics
technique: Counted-thread geometric needlework without knots (Gavanti line stitch, Murgi zigzag stitch)
gi_registration: GI Tagged under Karnataka Kasuti Embroidery
inclusive_growth_impact: Provides home-based micro-entrepreneurship for thousands of rural women artisans in Bagalkote
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal & Karnataka State Handicrafts Development Corporation (KSHDC)

name: Traditional Bagalkote Cuisine (Uttara Karnataka Oota)
description: Authentic North Karnataka culinary tradition centered on dry-land nutritious millets, legumes, and unique spice blends. The daily staple is Jolada Rotti (unleavened sorghum flatbread baked on terracotta or iron pans), paired with Ennegayi (spiced stuffed baby eggplants), Shenga Chutney Pudi (spicy groundnut powder with garlic and red chillies), Junka (spiced chickpea flour curry), and fresh curd.
location: Across all taluks of Bagalkote District (Badami, Bagalkote, Ilkal, Mudhol, Jamkhandi)
cultural_origin: Centuries-old agro-pastoral dietary tradition suited to the arid Deccan climate
key_dishes: Ennegayi / Badanekayi Palya (Stuffed baby aubergine in peanut-sesame gravy)
Shenga Chutney Pudi (Roasted groundnut garlic powder with flaxseed)
Kaalu Palya (Sprouted moth bean and whole green gram dry curries)
Girmit & Mirchi Bajji (Puffed rice evening snack with fried chilli fritters)
Amingad Kardant (Nutritious sweet made of edible gum, dry fruits, jaggery, and ghee from Amingad village)
Shenga Holige (Sweet flatbread stuffed with peanut and jaggery paste)
inclusive_growth_impact: Sustains local small-scale Khanavalis (traditional eateries) and rural women food cooperatives
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal & Karnataka Tourism

name: Amingad Kardant Sweet Tradition
description: A legendary energy-dense confectionery originating in the village of Amingad (Hunagund taluk) in Bagalkote district in the early 20th century. Prepared using fried edible gum (dink/antina), pure jaggery syrup, ghee, copra, and an abundance of dry fruits (almonds, cashews, pistachios).
cultural_origin: Pioneered in 1907 by confectioners in Amingad; traditionally offered to athletes, wrestlers, and new mothers
inclusive_growth_impact: Direct source of rural agro-processing employment and flagship souvenir product of the district
source: Official Bagalkote District Portal & Karnataka Tourism

name: Sharana Vachana Sahitya & Dasoha Tradition
description: The egalitarian Vachana literature tradition pioneered in the 12th century by Jagadjyothi Basaveshwara, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahadevi, and other Sharanas. Emphasizes Kayaka (honest labor as worship) and Dasoha (unconditional selfless service and community sharing of food and resources).
location: Kudala Sangama and throughout Bagalkote District
cultural_origin: 12th Century Kalyana Sharana Movement centered at Kudala Sangama
inclusive_growth_impact: Forms the spiritual ethos for universal inclusive growth, dignity of manual labor, and communal hospitality across Bagalkote
source: Kudalasangama Development Board & Official Bagalkote District Portal
